sn56.11:1.1: This is the Buddha’s first discourse proper. In the narrative following the Buddha’s awakening ([pli-tv-kd1:6.16.9]()), it follows the apparently fruitless encounter with Upaka ([mn26:25.1](), and precedes the teaching on not-self ([sn22.59]()). It is included in full in the later treatise the Paṭisambhidāmagga ([ps2.6:1.1]()), and is alluded to many times in the Suttas, sometimes by name ([mn141:32.1]()), sometimes implicitly ([mn26:29.1]()). It still forms the basis of education in Theravāda Buddhism, and is regularly memorized and recited.
sn56.11:9.1: The related passage at AN 8.64 suggests that the tiparivaṭṭaṁ dvādasākāraṁ apply to the knowledge, not the truths.
